catalogue.description: Joker (2019), directed by Todd Phillips and starring Joaquin Phoenix, Robert De Niro and Zazie Beetz, is a crime-drama thriller presented as a bleak character study and origin story. It follows a marginalized party clown and failed stand-up comedian who, amid poverty, illness, and social rejection, slips into violence and social unrest. The film combines gritty, period-inflected visuals with a psychological focus on trauma, identity, and class, delivering an intense, morally ambiguous emotional experience.

schedule.label: Open the room
schedule.activity: Invite each circle to introduce a familiar way into the program. Speculative fiction readers: Having and Being Had. Hip-hop listeners: Tyler, the Creator.

schedule.label: Read: Having and Being Had
schedule.activity: Host-selected material: Introduce Having and Being Had through ownership and belonging. Ask guests to name an object that signals belonging. schedule.label: Listen: Tyler, the Creator
schedule.activity: Host-selected recording: EARFQUAKE, the 2019 IGOR studio recording by Tyler, the Creator. Discuss its public persona; no playback is assumed. Ask what detail connects or contrasts with the book introduction.

schedule.label: Discuss: Joker

Compare one example from each work, then say where the comparison breaks. Invite each circle to contribute an example or disagreement. The host's interpretation is separate from Qloo ranks.

scoring.explanation: For each circle and domain, every candidate is ranked against the same shortlist. Relative score = 100 × (shortlist size - rank + 1) / shortlist size. Missing candidates receive 0 as a conservative evidence gap. A circle coverage score is the mean across the three slots. The agent maximizes the lowest circle coverage, then the average. These are application-derived rank scores, not Qloo probabilities, measured satisfaction, attendance, or revenue.

catalogue.description: Blindspotting (2018), directed by Carlos López Estrada and written by Daveed Diggs and Rafael Casal, is a comedy-crime-drama starring Daveed Diggs, Rafael Casal, and Janina Gavankar. The film follows a man trying to finish his last three days of probation while his friendship with a volatile coworker is tested after a nearby police shooting in Oakland. The result is emotionally urgent, often unsettling, and politically resonant.

Radiohead are an English alternative rock band formed in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, in 1985. The five-member group—Thom Yorke, Jonny Greenwood, Colin Greenwood, Ed O'Brien and Philip Selway—rose from the breakthrough single "Creep" and early guitar-driven rock to become celebrated for ambitious, genre-defying albums (OK Computer, Kid A, In Rainbows). They blend rock, electronic, orchestral and experimental influences, work closely with producer Nigel Godrich and artist Stanley Donwood, and are noted for both critical acclaim and commercial success worldwide.

Pixies are an American alternative rock band formed in Boston in 1986. Known for their loud-quiet-loud dynamics, surreal and often cryptic lyrics, and a blend of melodic hooks with abrasive guitar textures, they released seminal records including Come On Pilgrim (EP), Surfer Rosa, Doolittle, Bossanova and Trompe le Monde. They split in 1993, reunited in 2004 and have continued to record and tour with lineup changes (notably Kim Deal on bass and vocals until 2013, Paz Lenchantin 2016–2024, and Emma Richardson joining in 2024). Beck Hansen is an American singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist celebrated for eclectic, genre-blending music that mixes folk, hip-hop, electronic, rock and experimental pop. Rising from the early-90s anti-folk and underground scenes in Los Angeles and New York, he broke into the mainstream with the 1994 hit "Loser" and consolidated critical and commercial success with albums such as Odelay, Sea Change, Morning Phase and Colors. His work is marked by inventive sampling, ironic and poetic lyrics, diverse production approaches and frequent collaborations with producers and guest musicians

It follows a marginalized party clown and failed stand-up comedian who, amid poverty, illness, and social rejection, slips into violence and social unrest. The film combines gritty, period-inflected visuals with a psychological focus on trauma, identity, and class, delivering an intense, morally ambiguous emotional experience.
